state.repo: dhanesh/agent-skills: a collection of agent skills that together form a software factory (idea, spec, design, build, verify, review, release, operate, support, growth, knowledge, governance). A human orchestrates the stages.
state.rubric:
Status rubric. A row's status judges the stage's core job only. How work passes from one stage to the next is judged in the Stage handoffs row.

- `covered`: one or more skills do the stage's core job, and no limit weakens it.
- `covered, with limits`: the skills do the core job. The row names each limit that weakens the proof or leaves a step to you. A limit that you chose (launch, pricing, spend, merge, deploy, external messages) does not lower a row.
- `partly`: part of the core job has no skill. The row names that part after "Limits:".
- `missing`: no skill does the core job.
- `out of scope, by design`: the owner decided that the factory does not do this stage.

s_idea_validation.instructions: Judge the status of the stage 'Idea validation' of a software factory built from agent skills, using only the rubric in `rubric`. What the skills do for this stage, and their limits: `idea-validation` turns an idea into a brief whose riskiest assumptions each carry a test, a metric, pass and kill thresholds and a deadline, registers it before any result, computes GO, KILL, STALLED or PENDING from the results you report, flags a critical assumption you drop later, and hands a `go` to `spec-first-planning` as an `idea-brief/v1` envelope. Limits: you run every experiment (the agent never publishes, sends or spends); results are claimed, not proven; the stage cannot run unattended

s_test_verify.instructions: Judge the status of the stage 'Test / verify' of a software factory built from agent skills, using only the rubric in `rubric`. What the skills do for this stage, and their limits: `verifier-installer`, `test-safety-net`; `verification-skill-forge` generates a verify skill that drives the running app and records SHA-bound evidence, which `factory-conductor`'s evidence gate requires before a merge. A feature can also state a contract whose clauses carry a stronger proof: `proved` (Verus), `bounded` (Kani) or `property` (proptest, Hypothesis, fast-check, rapid), with a caught mutant for the last two. A plan's `[tier: ...]` hint sets the weakest tier the gate accepts. Limits: no `proved` or `bounded` backend for Python, TypeScript or Go yet, and verifier-installer does not detect proof backends yet

s_operate_planning.instructions: Judge the status of the stage 'Operate → planning' of a software factory built from agent skills, using only the rubric in `rubric`. What the skills do for this stage, and their limits: `ops-intake` reads failed releases, failing CI on the default branch, GitHub issues and (through a JSON-lines transform) Jira or Linear, ranks them into a local queue, and hands the item you pick to `spec-first-planning` as an `intake-item/v1` envelope; a verified release that holds the fix marks it resolved. Limits: on demand only; it cannot enforce that MCP calls are read-only; squash merges and partial runs need your manual `resolve`; Jira and Linear come in through documented conversion recipes, not dedicated readers

s_growth_monetise.instructions: Judge the status of the stage 'Growth / monetise' of a software factory built from agent skills, using only the rubric in `rubric`. What the skills do for this stage, and their limits: `growth-review` checks the metrics you export against warn and breach thresholds you register before the data comes in, reports OK, WARN, BREACH or NO_DATA per metric for the last complete UTC period, keeps judging on the registered thresholds when the plan is edited afterwards (`+stale`), and sends each breach to `ops-intake` through `intake-signals-jsonl`. Limits: you export the data and set the thresholds; launch and pricing stay manual (the agent never publishes, emails, changes a price or spends); the money ledger is in `factory-conductor`; no forecasts or statistics
